GitHub advisory GHSA-x746-7m8f-x49c and CVE.org CVE-2026-48817 (cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED, not rejected/withdrawn; GHSA withdrawn_at null) describe HTTPEndpoint selecting a handler by lowercasing the client HTTP method and invoking getattr without restricting to known verbs. Source-to-sink at 1.0.0/1.0.1: Route(..., methods=None) on a class endpoint leaves self.methods=None, so Route.matches returns FULL and Route.handle forwards every method; HTTPEndpoint.dispatch then does handler_name = request.method.lower() (HEAD->GET unless head exists) and getattr(self, handler_name, self.method_not_allowed). A token such as _DO_DELETE therefore invokes _do_delete, bypassing checks on the intended public handler. The same unconstrained getattr first appears in PR #52 member dd11c69b5b115bc97b7139c59fbd1dd555c4fbde (starlette/views.py View.dispatch: request_method from request.method, then getattr(self, request_method.lower(), None); func(request)). At that commit Path.methods defaults to () and Path.__call__ only rejects when self.methods is truthy, so a non-standard method already reached the view.
